minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard library, Council on Aging and school FY16 requests; the school ask far exceeds revenue growth.
minutes.summary: The committee continued departmental budget reviews, hearing the library, the Council on Aging and the school superintendent. The superintendent presented a recommended budget well above the town target, including about 20 new positions, and a member asked how to reconcile it with projected revenue growth. Minutes for two earlier meetings were approved, the standing agenda item was renamed, and the schedule through the March 26 hearing was set.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented a recommended FY16 school budget above the town target, and a member asked how to reconcile it with projected revenue growth.
A member noted the school request exceeds projected town revenue growth and asked how the two could be reconciled.
The Council on Aging director presented the department budget and asked for more staffing and for the programming line the town manager cut to be restored.
The library director presented the FY16 request, with the increase mostly in utilities; the town manager's recalculated utility figures may be lower.
The committee renamed a standing agenda item and set the schedule through the March 26 budget hearing and final votes.

why_it_matters: The school request is the largest pressure on the FY16 town budget, and if it is funded above revenue growth, the gap would have to be met by cuts elsewhere or by higher taxes.
Library and Council on Aging requests, including utility costs and a cut programming line, are still open and will be settled at the March 26 budget hearing and final votes.
watch_next: March 12: DPW and Monty Tech budget reviews.
March 26: budget hearing and final committee votes, after a special meeting on March 19.
